`final class ShaderPipeline`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.shader.pipeline` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [ShaderPipeline.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/shader/pipeline/ShaderPipeline.java)

Draws something into an offscreen framebuffer, runs it through a chain of shader passes, and draws the result in place.

## Description

A node effect such as a blur or a rounded mask goes through it; call it yourself in a node layer or a custom node ([Post-process with shader passes](/use/learn/going-further/shaders/#post-process-with-shader-passes)).

The area grows by the largest [`IShaderPass.expansion`](/reference/shaders/ishaderpass/#IShaderPass-method-expansion) of the passes, and only its part visible on screen is rendered, at the resolution of the screen.
Each pass reads the result of the previous one; the last pass draws on screen with premultiplied blending.
The framebuffers come from [`FrameBufferPool`](/reference/drawing/framebufferpool/), a pair per nesting depth, so a pipeline inside a pass gets its own.

## Method details

<a id="ShaderPipeline-method-render"></a>

### render

`void render(double x, double y, double width, double height, Runnable baseDraw, IShaderPass... passes)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Runs `baseDraw` into the area at `x`, `y` of `width` × `height`, in the coordinates you draw in, then applies `passes` in order.
Without passes, or with an area of no width or height, it runs `baseDraw` directly.

`void render(double x, double y, double width, double height, Runnable baseDraw, List<IShaderPass> passes)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Runs `baseDraw` into the area at `x`, `y` of `width` × `height`, then applies the passes of the list in order, as the varargs form does.
